title: ～かしら — “I wonder ～” (feminine)
summary: かしら is a sentence-final expression meaning “I wonder if ～.” It voices a question to yourself or a soft question to a close listener. It is traditionally used by women, and men use かな instead.

patterns.form: 動詞・い形容詞の普通形 ＋ かしら
patterns.gloss: 晴れる → 晴れるかしら / 合う → 合うかしら

patterns.form: 名詞・な形容詞（だ を除く）＋ かしら
patterns.gloss: 本当かしら / 大丈夫かしら

body.p: It combines the question か with しら, from 知らぬ (“do not know”). The sense is “I don't know whether ～.”
Use it to say a question to yourself, almost like thinking aloud: 明日は晴れるかしら. It can also make an indirect request, as in ～てくれないかしら. Nouns and na-adjectives take no だ.
It is conversational and does not suit writing or formal speech. Men normally use かな for the same meaning, and かしら has a feminine feel.

examples.ja: 明日（あした）は晴（は）れるかしら。
examples.tr: I wonder if it will be sunny tomorrow.

examples.ja: この服（ふく）、私（わたし）に合（あ）うかしら。
examples.romaji: Kono fuku, watashi ni au kashira.
examples.tr: I wonder if these clothes suit me.

examples.ja: もう電車（でんしゃ）は行（い）ってしまったかしら。
examples.romaji: Mō densha wa itte shimatta kashira.
examples.tr: I wonder if the train has already left.

pitfalls: Do not put だ before it: 本当かしら, not 本当だかしら.
Men, writing and conversations with superiors normally use かな or でしょうか instead.
